svg.aria-label: When to change a flat tire yourself and when to call: change it only on a wide right shoulder or off the freeway entirely, never on the left shoulder or in a lane; a donut spare is limited to about 50 mph and a short distance; call for a tow instead when the sidewall is shredded, there is no spare, the locking lug nut key is missing, or the wheel is damaged
svg.text: Flat on I-80: the shoulder decides, not the tire
Look at where the car is sitting before you open the trunk

g.text: You are off the freeway, or the right
shoulder is wide with no barrier
You have a real spare, the jack and the lug key
Sidewall shredded, or no spare at all
The wheel is bent, or a stud has sheared
Narrow shoulder, a barrier, or the left side
What a donut spare is actually rated for
and a short run, often quoted as 70 miles
Read the sticker on the spare itself
Braking and handling are worse until it is off

svg.text: Many cars built in the last fifteen years carry sealant and a pump instead of a spare, which cannot fix a blowout
